steps.text: Whisk sugar, cocoa, and flour in a medium bowl until no lumps remain.
Pour in milk and whisk until well combined.
Transfer mixture to a saucepan; cook and stir over medium heat until it thickens to a gravy consistency, 7 to 10 minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in butter and vanilla.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern-Style Chocolate Gravy
raw_recipe.description: This chocolate gravy is lusciously smooth and easy to make with basic pantry ingredients. Delicious served on top of hot and flaky homemade biscuits.

video.description: This southern-favorite recipe is your excuse to have chocolate for breakfast. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make southern-style chocolate gravy over the stove with only a handful of ingredients! Served over freshly baked buttery biscuits, the gravy strikes the perfect balance of sweetness without being too overwhelming.
video.name: How to Make Southern-Style Chocolate Gravy

review.reviewBody: This is exactly same recipe handed down through generations of my mother's southern family. We've never had it written down, so there's always too much inconsistency and variation. Thanks for putting measurements to this! I do always add a dash of salt and a bit more butter to mine than is called for here. When I was a little girl, all my friends wanted to spend the night so they could have Chocolate Gravy for breakfast. My kids have introduced several of their friends to it as well....looks like the tradition is in no danger of dying out anytime soon!
came out silky smooth and perfect! I did add the 1/4 tsp salt and used a half cup cocoa, awesome!!!!

I grew up on chocolate gravy. Both my mother and grandmother made it, but never recorded a recipe. I make this recipe every Christmas for our family. Doubled the recipe, added a few shakes of salt, and more butter. Sifted ingredients together prior to adding the milk and stirred continuously. It is delicious. My son-in-law suggested adding a bit of coffee next time around. Might try that.

This is pretty much perfect. I added some salt to complement the sweetness, but overall flavor was good. I thought it was odd to put butter in at the end, but following the instructions will give you a nice smooth, saucy gravy that is just thin enough to ladle over biscuits. I made this for Christmas Eve breakfast and I thought my in-laws were going to lick the pan. The second time I made this I tried starting with a roux (more like traditional gravy) and found the butter to powder ratio isn’t quite right for that and I ended up with lumps. Just follow the recipe.
Added jimmy dean sausage to recipe , venison sausage is even better. Did saute sausage first before adding. Add the sausage drippings as well ,even a little bacon grease kicks it up 10 stars 😋
My husband loves this recipe! I substituted with all purpose gluten free flour because that's what I had on hand, and reduced sugar from 3/4 cup down to 1/4 cup. Still sweet enough for him!
I have made this a few times. My kid and I love it. I will add in a tablespoon of strong coffee if I have it: it just enhances chocolate flavor.
I substituted hot cocoa mix for cocoa powder and it tastes heavenly! Thanks for sharing this recipe with us!
Just added 1/2 cup cocoa and did add salt. Turned out great. Will make it again.

I live in the Midwest, and have never had chocolate gravy before. I’m certainly not a connoisseur, but here’s my review. I did consider adding a pinch of salt, because it seemed like I should have, but I’m actually glad I didn’t. My biscuits already had salt in them, so I think adding salt to the gravy would have been too much. I did stir in a tablespoon or so of heavy cream just to thin it a little bit after it had cooled a bit. The flavor reminded me of those chocolate filled pies that you get out of the paper sleeve, but better because it didn’t have the preservatives. My kids and I all agreed 5 stars. It was absolutely delicious! We will make it again.
So easy and so delicious. My family's favorite gravy. I use 1\2 Splenda and 1\2 sugar to cut down on the carbs just a bit. I've tried with just Splenda and it really needs the sugar.

This is chocolate pudding. I kept thinking that as I was measuring out the ingredients. Once I made it, it was thin chocolate pudding. Well, who can complain about chocolate pudding for breakfast? I made chocolate gravy once twenty some years ago because my husband kept talking about his step mom making it when he was growing up, but I don't remember what I thought of it - probably because I prefer savory over sweet. The flavor is nice, and it tastes exactly like milk chocolate pudding, but it's odd with the biscuit as the biscuit is heavy and dense and not sweet. This belongs spooned over a sponge cake topped with fruit rather than on a breakfast biscuit. I'd rather have it as a dessert sauce. On a biscuit, I don't like it. As a sauce, it's fine.
Great as is
Loved it!

Haven’t had chocolate gravy and biscuits since my nana passed- unfortunately I never got the recipe from her. This was dang near identical to hers! It was so easy to make, I already had all the ingredients when I got the hankerin for it…as an Arkansan, I give this recipe the highest praise!!
My mother made this for all of us every Christmas morning. I am making it for my grandson tomarrow with baking soda biscuits, my kids loved it too.

So a few of the reviews made me worry. It's not supposed to be overly sweet its a Gravy. I thought it was really good and the perfect sweetness for a Gravy if you want to add it to something else add more sugar.

I've always heard of it but never tried. Me and mom were just watching recipes on YouTube, a regular event for us, lol. I love trying new recipes and experimenting with recipes! Anyways she popped up and said "OMG, I've not had that since was a kid!!" So I googled recipe and picked this one, since most my recipes I look up I always pick allrecipes. And OMG she is right! I love it! I'll definitely be saving this and making a lot more! Also sending it to my daughter right now! Thank you

So I was really excited to make this recipe because I can’t find my grandma’s. The more I stirred it out of the ingredients the more I realized it’s not chocolate gravy. It’s chocolate pie filling that’s all it is. It’s two egg yolks away from being a pie filling. Nice try but missed the mark way off!

My first time making homemade chocolate gravy (not my normal cook and serve chocolate pudding) and it turned out amazing!! I’ll definitely keep this recipe for future Breakfasts and Breakfast for Dinners!! Thanks for sharing!!!
